title: Comparative and superlative adjectives
summary: Степени сравнения без шаблонов: двусложные прилагательные, **the better of two**, усилители **much / far / by far**, **second-largest**, **the least**, **farther / further** и **elder / older**.
ru:
## Спорные случаи образования
Односложные прилагательные берут **-er/-est**, длинные — **more/most**. Продвинутый уровень — это двусложные слова, где работают оба способа:
> **clever, narrow, quiet, simple, gentle, common, pleasant, polite, handsome** — cleverer / more clever, quieter / more quiet.
- Слова на **-y** почти всегда меняют -y на -ier: **happier, funnier, easiest**.
- Слова на **-ed, -ing, -ful, -less, -ous, -ive** — только **more/most**: ~~wonderfuller~~ → **more wonderful**, ~~tireder~~ → **more tired**.
- Если сомневаетесь — **more/most** почти всегда безопасно, а вот «-er» у длинного слова — ошибка.

## the better of two и the best of three
Когда сравниваем **двоих**, формально используем сравнительную степень с **the**; суперлатив — для трёх и более.
> Of the two options, this one is **the more realistic**. — Из двух вариантов этот реалистичнее.
> She is **the taller** of the twins. — Она выше из близнецов.
> This is **the most realistic** of the three proposals. — Из трёх предложений это самое реалистичное.
В разговорной речи часто звучит и **the most/best of two**, но на экзамене и в письме выбирайте формальный вариант.

## Усиление и ослабление сравнения
Перед сравнительной степенью нельзя ставить **very** — только **much, far, a lot, a great deal, even, still, slightly, a bit, rather**.
> The new model is **far more efficient**. — Новая модель гораздо эффективнее.
> It's **slightly cheaper** than before. — Это чуть дешевле, чем раньше.
> ~~very better~~, ~~very more expensive~~ → **much better**, **much more expensive**
Перед суперлативом ставим **by far, easily, quite, almost, nearly**: *by far the best*, *easily the most important*, *nearly the oldest*.

## Суперлатив: полезные детали
- Предлог: **in** + место/группа (*in the company, in the world*), **of** + множество (*of all, of the three, of them*).
- **one of the + суперлатив + множественное число**: *one of the most useful tools*.
- **ever / I've ever seen** — типичное завершение: *the best film I've ever seen*.
- Порядковые числительные: **the second-largest** city, **the third-highest** peak.
- **least** — зеркало most: *the least reliable*, *the least expensive*; **less ... than**.
> Без **the** в значении «очень»: *It was **most** kind of you.* — Это было очень любезно с вашей стороны (это не суперлатив).

## Особые формы
> **farther / further** — расстояние; **further** ещё и «дополнительный»: *further information*.
> **older / elder** — **elder** только перед существительным в семье: *my elder sister* (без than).
> **later / latter** — «позже» и «последний из двух»; **latest / last** — «самый новый» и «последний».
> **nearest / next** — ближайший по расстоянию / следующий по очереди.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~more taller~~ → **taller** (двойное сравнение)
- ~~the most unique~~ → **unique** (абсолютное прилагательное; допустимо *rather unusual*)
- ~~Anna is the cleverest of the two.~~ → Anna is **the cleverer** of the two.
- ~~It was very worse than I expected.~~ → It was **much worse** than I expected.
en:
## Tricky formation
Short adjectives take **-er/-est**, longer ones take **more/most**. At this level the difficult group is two-syllable adjectives that can use both:
> **clever, narrow, quiet, simple, gentle, common, pleasant, polite, handsome** — cleverer / more clever, quieter / more quiet.
- Adjectives ending in **-y** nearly always change to **-ier / -iest**: **happier, funnier, easiest**.
- Words ending in **-ed, -ing, -ful, -less, -ous, -ive** only take **more/most**: ~~wonderfuller~~ → **more wonderful**, ~~tireder~~ → **more tired**.
- When in doubt, **more/most** is almost always safe; adding -er to a long word is an error.

## the better of two and the best of three
When we compare **two** things, formal English uses the comparative with **the**; the superlative is for three or more.
> Of the two options, this one is **the more realistic**.
> She is **the taller** of the twins.
> This is **the most realistic** of the three proposals.
In casual speech people often say **the most/best of two**, but in formal writing and exams use the formal pattern.

## Strengthening and softening a comparison
Before a comparative we cannot use **very**; we use **much, far, a lot, a great deal, even, still, slightly, a bit, rather**.
> The new model is **far more efficient**.
> It's **slightly cheaper** than before.
> ~~very better~~, ~~very more expensive~~ → **much better**, **much more expensive**
Before a superlative we use **by far, easily, quite, almost, nearly**: *by far the best*, *easily the most important*, *nearly the oldest*.

## Useful details about the superlative
- Prepositions: **in** + place/group (*in the company, in the world*), **of** + a set (*of all, of the three, of them*).
- **one of the + superlative + plural noun**: *one of the most useful tools*.
- **ever / I've ever seen** often ends the phrase: *the best film I've ever seen*.
- Ordinals: **the second-largest** city, **the third-highest** peak.
- **least** is the mirror of most: *the least reliable*, *the least expensive*; **less ... than**.
> Without **the**, **most** can mean 'very': *It was **most** kind of you.* (not a superlative)

## Special forms
> **farther / further** — distance; **further** also means 'additional': *further information*.
> **older / elder** — **elder** only before a noun in a family: *my elder sister* (not with than).
> **later / latter** — 'after' and 'the second of two'; **latest / last** — 'most recent' and 'final'.
> **nearest / next** — closest in distance / following in order.

## Common mistakes
- ~~more taller~~ → **taller** (double comparison)
- ~~the most unique~~ → **unique** (an absolute adjective; say *rather unusual* instead)
- ~~Anna is the cleverest of the two.~~ → Anna is **the cleverer** of the two.
- ~~It was very worse than I expected.~~ → It was **much worse** than I expected.
structure:
## Формулы
> короткое: adj + **-er / -est** (long → longer → **the longest**)
> длинное: **more / most** + adj (reliable → **more reliable** → **the most reliable**)
> «меньше»: **less / the least** + adj (**the least expensive**)
> сравнение: comparative + **than** + ...
> суперлатив: **the** + superlative + **in / of** + ...; + **(that) I've ever** + причастие II
> усилитель: **much / far / a lot / slightly** + comparative; **by far / easily** + the + superlative

## Таблица: нерегулярные и особые
| Прилагательное | Сравнит. | Превосх. | Заметка |
|---|---|---|---|
| good | **better** | **the best** | нерегулярное |
| bad | **worse** | **the worst** | нерегулярное |
| far | **farther / further** | **the farthest / furthest** | further = ещё |
| old | **older / elder** | **the oldest / eldest** | elder — о семье |
| late | **later / latter** | **the latest / last** | разные значения |
| little | **less** | **the least** | неисчисляемые |

exercises.title: Степени сравнения
exercises.instruction: Поставьте прилагательное из скобок в нужную степень сравнения (вместе с more / most / the, если нужно, — кроме того, что уже есть в тексте).
exercises.example: This route is (short). → This route is **shorter**.

items.text: The mountain road is {{shorter}}, but the coastal one is {{more scenic}}.
Of the two candidates, Sam is the {{more experienced}}.
It was {{the worst}} storm in the region for fifty years.
Rents are slightly {{higher}} than they were last year.
She is {{the most talented}} musician I have ever taught.
Could you speak a bit {{more slowly|slower}}?
That was {{the least}} interesting lecture of the term.
Which is {{the farthest|the furthest}} planet from the sun?

exercises.title: Детали суперлатива
exercises.instruction: Вставьте одно слово: **of, in, ever, far, the**.

items.text: He is one {{of}} the most respected scientists in the field.
She is the youngest professor {{in|at}} the university.
The new model is the lightest {{of}} the three.
It was the most exciting match we have {{ever}} seen.
This is by far {{the}} most difficult exam I've taken.
It was by {{far}} the longest meeting of the year.
Of the two proposals, this is {{the}} more realistic.
This is the best coffee I have {{ever}} tasted.

exercises.title: Выберите вариант
exercises.instruction: Выберите правильный вариант (в формальном письменном стиле).

items.q: Her new novel is ___ than her first one.
Of the two options, the second is ___.
It was ___ day of the whole trip.
He is ___ taller than his brother.
That's ___ the best restaurant in town.
items.why: Перед суперлативом — **by far**; very и a lot так не используются.

items.q: This is ___ of the two designs.
The speech was ___ more convincing than I'd expected.
items.why: **far more** — гораздо более; very не сочетается.

items.q: He's the ___ person I'd ask for help.
items.why: **the last person I'd ask** — последний, к кому я бы обратился (то есть ни за что не обращусь); latest — «самый новый», latter — «второй из двух».

options: She is more taller than me.
My brother is the most cleverest of us.
My brother is the clevererest of us.
My brother is the cleverest of us.
items.why: Суперлатив от clever образуется суффиксом: **the cleverest**; most + -est вместе не употребляются.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя степени сравнения.

items.prompt: What is the best film or book you've ever seen or read, and why?
items.sample: The best book I've ever read is a novel about a lighthouse keeper; it is far more moving than most books I know.

items.prompt: Compare two cities or places you know (use much / slightly / far).
items.sample: Almaty is much bigger than my hometown, but my hometown is slightly quieter.

items.prompt: Name the oldest and the youngest person in your family.
items.sample: My grandmother is the oldest person in my family, and my cousin Leyla is the youngest.

items.prompt: What is the least enjoyable thing you have to do each week?
items.sample: The least enjoyable thing I do each week is the grocery shopping on Saturday.
